protocol.name: sherlock_clipboard_v1

description.summary: the clipboard history, for the Super + V panel of the shell

protocol.description:
Private protocol between the compositor and the clipboard history panel of the shell (lot D-42). The compositor keeps what is copied in Wayland and X11 applications; this protocol lists it and acts on it. Like sherlock_shell_v1, its global is only offered to the clients of the shell socket (ADR 0021): no application can read the history nor put an item back.
Putting an item back makes it the clipboard again; the user then pastes it (ADR 0030).
Versioning follows sherlock_shell_v1: a backward compatible change adds requests, events or enum entries and bumps the version; an incompatible one renames the interface with a new suffix.

interface.name: sherlock_clipboard_history_v1
interface.description:
Once bound, the compositor sends the state event, an item event for every item kept, each followed by its thumbnail when it has one, then done. After that, it sends the changes as they happen: new or changed items, removed items, the state, each batch ended by done. A client applies what it received at done.
The client orders the items itself: pinned items first, then by time, newest first, and by id, highest first, for the same time.

entry.name: files
entry.summary: files, copied in a file manager

request.name: paste

description.summary: put an item back on the clipboard

request.description: The item of this id becomes the clipboard again, offered to Wayland and X11 applications in every type it was read as, and moves to the top. An unknown id, or a locked session, does nothing.

request.name: set_pinned
request.description: A pinned item is never removed to make room, nor by clear. Pinned: 1, else 0.

description.summary: forget every item but the pinned ones

event.name: state

description.summary: whether the history keeps the copies

event.description: 1 when the history is on, 0 when the user turned it off in Control Room: then the compositor keeps nothing, and lists nothing.

event.name: item

description.summary: an item is new or changed

event.description: The id stays the item's for as long as the compositor runs. The preview is a few lines, 300 characters at most: the text, the address, the paths of the files one per line, or the size of a picture. app is the app_id or X11 class of the window it was copied from, empty when unknown. time is when it was copied, last, in seconds since the Unix epoch.

event.name: thumbnail
event.description: A PNG of size bytes, 160 pixels on its longest side at most, from the start of a read-only file. Sent after the item event of the picture.

description.summary: end of a batch of changes
